### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 54 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ba87a50759b2776eaea0fc5e649fa67c0e959225` — the merge of head `987b7e72531b18326315a7c2d6f77d8053af5c2a` into base `1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ba87a50759b2776eaea0fc5e649fa67c0e959225 && git checkout ba87a50759b2776eaea0fc5e649fa67c0e959225
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55 987b7e72531b18326315a7c2d6f77d8053af5c2a && git checkout -B drift-repro 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55 && git merge --no-ff 987b7e72531b18326315a7c2d6f77d8053af5c2a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · REWORK (1 item, docs only)** · head `d3c32ee1cc975ea3ffa747f22a32deace0a95208` · card #33113 · read 2026-11-17T00:48Z

### REWORK

1. **The docs leave out two answers the door now gives.** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` › Bulk Import Users, checked sentence by sentence against `admin-import-users.ts`:
   - `rows[].positions` is documented as a list of outcomes, but a cell that is not a list answers the **string** `'unreadable'` (`r.positions = 'unreadable'`), and `summary.positions` counts that row under `unresolved` (`positionLinks.unresolved++`; pinned at `admin-import-users-manager-pass.test.ts:783-785`). A client that reads `rows[].positions` as an array breaks on it, so the page has to say both: the string value, and which counter it lands in.
   - Only the `501` whole-request refusal is documented. The `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` refusal, nothing created and dry runs included, when the caller's own access does not resolve (`seam.resolveActorContext()` answering nothing; pinned at `:828-836`) is missing.
   Docs-only; the changeset already names `'unreadable'` and both refusals and needs no change.

### The open question in the report (whole-request 501 / 403 before any write)

L1 reads option A as inside ruling 6920428750, not a new fork. The ruling's per-row clause covers a position that does not resolve or whose assignment is refused; a host with no grant seam, or a caller whose own access does not resolve, is known before the first write and would refuse every position on every row. A matches the sibling door: `import-sso-users` settles its grant seam and actor context before writing and answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` without one (`pending-sso-users.ts:290-310`), as create-user does (`admin-user-endpoints.ts:820-850`). Recorded here so it is visible to the maintainer's veto; not put to the decision box.

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, attribution header then `Fixes #33113`. Closing-keyword scan of the whole body: one hit, `#33113`; `#34535`, `#34536`, `#34537` follow `Filed:` / `filed:` with no keyword. `Fixes` is right: the ruled scope (one `positions` column, second pass, Setup's checks, per-row outcome, no permission-set column) is all in the diff.
- **File surface:** 22 files from `get_files`, inside claim 6931355877 and amendments 6931386726, 6931474183 (supersedes the `pending-sso-users.ts` export with the new `name-list-cell.ts`; the console list in `IdentityImportPanels.tsx`; the 11 locale lines) and 6932377459 (the two census artefacts). The `ui/` test `identityImportFields.emailRule-11913.test.tsx` pins the claimed panel. `auth-plugin.ts`: one line, `createGrant: createGrantFor(c)`.
- **Shared file:** `auth-plugin.ts` with open PR #34333. My own `git merge-tree --write-tree` of this head against `refs/pull/34333/head`: exit 0, no conflict.
- **Moved code:** `readNameList` moved byte for byte from `pending-sso-users.ts` into `name-list-cell.ts`, which the package index does not re-export; no new public name.
- **Security path:** the grant is a `sys_user_position` insert under the importing admin's context from `seam.resolveActorContext()`, never `SYSTEM_CTX`; ablation 1 (written as `SYSTEM_CTX`) turns 3 cases red because the test double refuses only non-system writes. The only `SYSTEM_CTX` read is the `already_assigned` probe for upserted rows, which writes nothing.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/33113-import-users-positions-column.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@object-ui/i18n` (both published) patch, `@object-ui/app-shell` (private) patch. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: a REST import column, no `authorable-surface` / `authorable-defaults` shard moves. Sentences checked: "assigned after every row of the batch has landed" (the pass runs after `runImport`); "the user is still created"; "a cell that is not a list reads 'unreadable'"; "501 … 403 … with nothing created, dry runs included" (the settlement precedes `runImport`); "Dry runs do not assign".
- **Docs (checked sentences other than item 1):** "the same column `import-sso-users` reads", "written under the importing admin's own access", "the user is still created", the four outcome names, "only adds positions", "dry runs do not assign": each true of the diff.
- **Rejection assertions:** `501` and `403` cases assert `status` and `error.code`; the per-row `refused` outcome asserts its `code`.
- **Tests and controls:** 11 new cases; ablations 1–3 with their red counts (3, 6, 7). Suites: plugin-auth 280 files / 5774 tests; ui 105 files / 1924 tests.
- **Gates at this head:** check-runs on `d3c32ee1…`: 72 runs, 61 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 failed; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` `success`. Derived-gate round 111/111.
- **Out of scope placed:** #34535 (multi-org imported users have no membership, so positions refuse), #34536 (wizard has no `manager_id` target), #34537 (skills card).

### Owed after this

- **L2: owed, `TIER_DEFAULT`**, on `Clause-②: yes (widening)` alone (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no narrowing, no governed path): the lane seat writes it. It pins a head; item 1 is docs-only, so it can run on the fixed head.
- **Landing tier:** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34531`: 0 of 22 paths governed, 625 changed lines (+580 / −45) ≤ 3000 ⇒ ordinary queue landing by the area after L1 ACCEPT and L2 PASS on the same head. Whichever of this PR and #34333 lands second re-reads the `auth-plugin.ts` intersection on its landing head.

### Next

L1 reads the delta only, on a head whose CI is green and announced final in a PR comment.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `987b7e72531b18326315a7c2d6f77d8053af5c2a`
Local-runs: none

The face is the declaration only: `record-recognisers --paths` decides no schema or rules face on the PR's paths (no `packages/spec/src`, no governed path), and the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line leaves the declaration face. Read: card #33113 and ruling 6920428750, the claim and its surface amendments, the net diff against the merge base, the r3 delta, and the head's check-runs (72: 61 success, 11 skipped, none failed or pending).

### ① Derived judgments

- `admin-import-users.ts`: the `positions` cell is read with `readNameList` and stripped before the identity write, as `manager_id` is, so `createUser` receives exactly what it received on `main`. The second pass runs after `runImport`, only for rows whose own write landed (`created` / `updated`), and never on a dry run. Right.
- Each assignment is one `sys_user_position` insert under the calling administrator's own context (`createGrant.resolveActorContext()`, the seam create-user and the pending doors use), never `SYSTEM_CTX`; the refusal is classified (`reference_not_found` on `position` ⇒ `unresolved`, else `refused` with the thrown code), never re-worded. The only `SYSTEM_CTX` use is the read of an existing hold on an upserted row, which writes nothing. Right.
- r3: no seam ⇒ every named position `refused` / `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on its row; no resolved context ⇒ `refused` / `PERMISSION_DENIED`; the users land in both cases, nothing is written to `sys_user_position`, `rows[].ok`, `rows[].code` and `summary.errors` are untouched. This matches ruling 6920428750's "per-row error, the user is still created". Right.
- `name-list-cell.ts` is a byte-for-byte move of `pending-sso-users.ts`'s `readNameList`, so the SSO import door reads its cells as before. `auth-plugin.ts` wires the same `createGrantFor(c)` the create-user door already gets. Right.
- UI: one `positions` target field in the Users import wizard and one hint string in every i18n pack. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

FROM, measured on `main` (the PR's FROM control test pins it): a file with a `positions` column answers `200`, creates its users and drops the cell. On this head the same file answers `200`, creates the same users, and now also assigns the positions or reports why not on the row. A file without the column takes no new branch (`positionsWanted` is all `undefined`, so neither the seam nor the pass is read). The response and the audit row only gain keys (`rows[].positions`, `summary.positions`). Nothing `main` accepted is refused; the r2 whole-file `501` / `403`, which narrowed this input, is withdrawn. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no metadata author writes anything new. The changeset is `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n` and carries both declaration lines. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- N1 (not blocking): `resolveActorContext()` is awaited before `runImport`. If it throws (an infrastructure fault while resolving the caller's session, not an unresolved principal, which answers `undefined`), the request fails before any user is written, where `main` would have created them. The create-user door shares this seam and this failure mode, and the caller's session has already been resolved once by the endpoint's own gate, so no input that `main` accepts is refused by contract. Hardening it to a per-row `refused` is a follow-up, not a reason to hold this PR.
- N2 (cosmetic): the wizard's `positions` field label is the literal `'Positions'`, not passed through `label()` like its siblings; `positions` is no `sys_user` field, so `label()` would have no field label to read.
- Multi-organization mode: the membership refusal answers each position `refused` / `VALIDATION_FAILED`, users created; filed as #34535 and named in the body.
- Generated census tables moved by one (`sys_user_position` insert call site), rewritten by the generator in the same commit.
- No open questions; no security finding.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The existing-hold read is one keyed `find` per position on upserted rows only (`limit: 1`), no id materialisation or in-app join.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-7l0awc`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmRXuRn93HphKp7kXEz`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

**L1 delta · ACCEPT** · head `987b7e72531b18326315a7c2d6f77d8053af5c2a` (delta over `d3c32ee1`, my REWORK 6934156935) · card #33113 · read 2026-11-17T02:54Z

### My earlier judgment of option A is superseded

In 6934156935 I read option A (refuse the whole file `501` / `403` before any write) as inside ruling 6920428750. That was wrong. On `main` the same file answers `200`, creates the users and silently drops the column (FROM measured on `d4c0c1210`, body › Acceptance notes), so A refused an input `main` accepts: a narrowing that `Clause-②: yes (widening)` did not declare. This head drops A for per-row outcomes, which is the ruling's own direction for a position that cannot be assigned. One wording nit for the body: "first ruled **A**" was an L1 reading, not a ruling.

### Delta read (3 commits of the PR's own and two merges of `main`)

- **REWORK item 1, closed** (`5185e099`, docs). The page now says `rows[].positions` is an array, except the **string** `'unreadable'` for a cell that is not a list, which counts once under `summary.positions.unresolved` with the user still created. Both match `admin-import-users.ts` (`r.positions = 'unreadable'`, `positionLinks.unresolved++`). The 403 sentence the item asked for became moot when r3 removed the 403.
- **r3 code (`4ed4e51c`, `admin-import-users.ts`)**, read in the source:
  - Both whole-request `fail(501…)` and `fail(403…)` are gone.
  - The seam and the actor context are read only when the run is not a dry run and a row names a list of positions. Exactly one of `grant` or `grantBlocked` (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with no seam, `PERMISSION_DENIED` with no context) is set.
  - The second pass sits inside the `if (!prepared.dryRun)` post-write block, so the non-null `grant!` is never reached without one of the two.
  - On `grantBlocked` each named position is `{ outcome: 'refused', code }`, `summary.positions.refused` grows by the count, and `rows[].error` is set once when empty. That is the same shape the existing refused-assignment branch uses. `ok`, `rows[].code` and `summary.errors` are untouched, and no `sys_user_position` insert runs.
  - `'unreadable'` rows keep their own branch ahead of it.
  - The docblocks (`IdentityImportDeps.createGrant`, `ImportPositionOutcome.refused`, the header list) say the same thing.
- **Tests (`admin-import-users-manager-pass.test.ts`, 11 → 13 cases).**
  - The two whole-request cases are removed. That is a change of behaviour the PR itself introduced, not a weakening of a pin on `main`.
  - The FROM control asserts `200`, `created: 2`, `errors: 0`, `createUser` called twice, and both rows `[true, 'created']`.
  - The no-seam case asserts each row's `positions` with `code: 'NOT_IMPLEMENTED'`, `rows[].code` undefined, a row with no positions untouched, `summary.positions` `{0, 0, 0, refused: 3}` and zero position inserts.
  - The no-context case asserts `200`, the user created, `ok: true`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` per position, `refused: 2` and zero inserts.
  - The no-seam dry run asserts `200`, no `positions`, and all-zero counters.
  - Both r3 ablations are recorded with their red counts (whole-file `501` restored: the FROM control and the `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` case; `grantBlocked && false`: the two per-row cases), each restored to the HEAD blob.
- **Docs and changeset (`e9211280`).** `authentication.mdx` › Bulk Import Users and the changeset now read: "the users are still created and every named position is reported `refused` on its row: `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` … `PERMISSION_DENIED` … Dry runs do not assign". That is true of the code above. A scan of the page and the changeset finds no sentence left over from the whole-file refusal ("nothing created", "no one was imported", a `501` / `403` for this door). The changeset's "Nothing that worked before is refused" now holds.
- **Declarations:** `Fixes #33113`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with no narrowing arm, and `Metadata-protocol: none`, all unchanged and right. The FROM paragraph records the withdrawn revision.
- **Merges:** the diff against the last merge's `main` parent is the same 22 files that `get_files` lists, at +659 / −45. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of this head against open PR #34333's head `9bb1e6ad` exits 0.
- **Gates at this head:** check-runs on `987b7e72…`: 72 runs, 61 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 failed. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Check Changeset` are all `success`. The derived-gate round is 111/111. The final head is announced in 6936546424.

The first-review checklist (6934156935) stands for everything outside this delta, except its paragraph on option A, which this verdict replaces.

### Owed after this

- **L2: owed, `TIER_DEFAULT`**, on `Clause-②: yes (widening)` alone; the lane seat writes it on this head. It should read the per-row refusal for a host that cannot judge the grant against ruling 6920428750.
- **Landing tier:** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34531`: 0 of 22 paths governed, 704 changed lines (+659 / −45) ≤ 3000. This is an ordinary queue landing by the area once the L2 PASS names this head. Whichever of this PR and #34333 lands second re-reads the `auth-plugin.ts` intersection on its landing head.
